mainTopic: The count of יהושע's ten conditions, and the reasons behind עזרא's ten תקנות
overview: The גמרא challenges the count of ten conditions of יהושע, because רבי יוחנן reports another condition about trees near a border and ביכורים. It answers that the number ten comes from רבי יהושע בן לוי, an אמורא, so רבי יוחנן may disagree. It also brings a version that names him openly. Next, the גמרא lists the ten תקנות of עזרא and explains them one by one: the שבת afternoon reading, Monday and Thursday reading, courts on Monday and Thursday, laundry on Thursday, garlic on ערב שבת, and early baking for the poor. A ברייתא proves that Monday and Thursday reading began with the נביאים in the desert. The answer is that עזרא set the format of three men reading ten פסוקים. Along the way, the גמרא adds a side ברייתא about the benefits of garlic. Finally, it asks how combing before טבילה can be עזרא's תקנה when the Torah already requires it. The answer begins on this amud: the Torah only requires checking the hair, and the rest continues on the next amud.

steps.title: An eleventh condition of Joshua?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says יהושע also set a condition about trees near a border and ביכורים, which seems to make more than ten conditions.
steps.simpleTranslation: But when רבי אבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a tree that leans into a neighbor's field and a tree near the border, the owner brings ביכורים and reads the declaration, because יהושע gave out the land on this condition!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim that יהושע made exactly ten conditions. רבי יוחנן reports another condition, which would make eleven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, someone whose tree draws nourishment from another person's land might not be able to say 'the land You gave me' in the ביכורים declaration. רבי יוחנן says יהושע set a condition so this is not a problem. That is a new condition beyond the ten listed.

keyTerms.meaning: A tree that leans over into someone else's field
He brings ביכורים and recites the declaration
Gave as an inheritance; divided the land

phrases.english: But when Rabbi Avin came
he said that Rabbi Yochanan says:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד אִילָן הַנּוֹטֶה לְתוֹךְ שְׂדֵה חֲבֵירוֹ,
phrases.english: Both a tree that leans into the field of another,
and a tree that is close to the boundary –
he brings and recites,
phrases.notes: He brings ביכורים from that tree and says the declaration in דברים 26:5–10.

phrases.english: for it was on this condition
that Joshua apportioned the land to Israel!
phrases.notes: This would be an extra condition, so how can the list say only ten?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier list of ten conditions of יהושע
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that יהושע made exactly ten conditions
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן cites another condition of יהושע, making the number more than ten

steps.title: The 'ten' list is from רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: The count of ten comes from רבי יהושע בן לוי, an אמורא, so רבי יוחנן can disagree and add more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, who taught the ten conditions of יהושע? It is רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by identifying who said 'ten.' It was רבי יהושע בן לוי, not an older authoritative source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the list were a ברייתא from a תנא, an אמורא like רבי יוחנן could not easily argue. But since an אמורא said it, two אמוראים can simply disagree about how many conditions there were.

phrases.english: Rather, who taught
the ten conditions that Joshua stipulated?
It is Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.
phrases.notes: He's an אמורא, like רבי יוחנן, so they're allowed to disagree.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: the count belongs to a single אמורא, allowing disagreement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The number ten was a fixed, authoritative tradition that no one could add to
steps.terutzMaskana: The count of ten is רבי יהושע בן לוי's view; רבי יוחנן holds there were more

steps.title: A version that names the source openly
steps.stepSummary: רב גביהה from בי כתיל teaches the statement with רבי יהושע בן לוי named directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גביהה from בי כתיל teaches it openly: רבי תנחום and רבי ברייס say in the name of a certain elder, and who is he? רבי יהושע בן לוי: יהושע made ten conditions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its answer. One teacher's version openly says the 'ten conditions' statement comes from רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 identified the source by reasoning. Here a teacher's actual version states it outright, confirming that the number ten is an אמורא's opinion.
steps.whatToRemember: The count of ten conditions of יהושע is רבי יהושע בן לוי's view, so רבי יוחנן can add another.

phrases.english: Rav Geviha from Bei Katil
teaches it explicitly:
Rabbi Tanchum and Rabbi Berayes
say in the name of a certain elder,
and who is he? Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi;
Joshua stipulated ten conditions.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב גְּבִיהָה מִבֵּי כְתִיל מַתְנֵי לַהּ בְּהֶדְיָא
steps.raayaObject: That the ten-conditions statement belongs to רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב גביהה's version, which names רבי יהושע בן לוי directly

steps.title: עזרא's ten ordinances
steps.stepSummary: A list of ten תקנות made by עזרא, covering reading the תורה, courts, preparing for שבת, women's practices, peddlers, and immersion.
steps.simpleTranslation: עזרא made ten תקנות: reading the תורה at מנחה on שבת; reading on Monday and Thursday; courts sitting on Monday and Thursday; laundering on Thursday; eating garlic on ערב שבת; a woman rising early to bake; a woman wearing a protective garment; a woman combing her hair before immersing; peddlers traveling through towns; and immersion for בעלי קריין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: a list of ten תקנות of עזרא. The next steps will explain each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list parallels the ten conditions of יהושע just discussed. The items are listed briefly here, and the גמרא will now go back and give the reason for each.

keyTerms.meaning: Men who had a seminal emission

phrases.english: Ezra instituted ten ordinances:
that they read the Torah at Mincha on Shabbat;
and they read on Monday and Thursday;
and the courts judge on Monday and Thursday;
and they launder on Thursday;
and they eat garlic on Shabbat eve;
and that a woman should rise early and bake;
and that a woman should wear a breechcloth;
and that a woman should comb her hair and then immerse;
and that peddlers should travel around the towns;
and he instituted immersion for those who had a seminal emission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new list, parallel to the ten conditions of יהושע

steps.title: Why the תורה is read at מנחה on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The first תקנה, reading at מנחה on שבת, was made for people who sit idle on street corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reading the תורה at מנחה on שבת was instituted because of those who sit on street corners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining עזרא's list, starting with the first item. It gives the reason for the שבת afternoon reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some people are busy or idle during the week and don't come to hear the תורה read. A reading on שבת afternoon, when they are free, gives them a chance to hear it.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who sit on street corners

phrases.english: That they should read at Mincha on Shabbat –
is because of those who sit on street corners.
phrases.notes: These are people who don't come to shul during the week to hear the תורה read.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first item in the list of step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שבת מנחה reading was instituted for those who miss the weekday readings

steps.title: Didn't Monday and Thursday תורה reading exist before עזרא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the second תקנה on the list. Reading the Torah on Monday and Thursday seems to have been set up long before עזרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that they should read on Monday and Thursday: did עזרא institute this? But it was already instituted from the very beginning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second item on עזרא's list and challenges it. It claims this practice is older than עזרא. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list said עזרא made the תקנה of reading on Monday and Thursday. The גמרא says this cannot be his תקנה if it already existed. Either the list is wrong, or עזרא added something new to the practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Monday and Thursday (literally, the second and fifth days of the week)
He instituted, he made a rabbinic enactment

phrases.english: And that they should read on Monday and Thursday:
Did Ezra institute this?!
But it was already instituted from the very beginning!

steps.triggerLanguage: עֶזְרָא תִּיקֵּן?! וְהָא מֵעִיקָּרָא הֲוָה מִיתַּקְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the first תקנה (reading at מנחה on שבת), the גמרא moves on to the second תקנה and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in עזרא's list that he instituted Torah reading on Monday and Thursday.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the practice already existed before עזרא, it cannot be counted as his new תקנה.

steps.title: The prophets in the desert set up Torah reading every few days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'no water' in the desert as 'no Torah.' It says the נביאים then set up reading on שבת, Monday and Thursday, so that three days would never pass without Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'And they went three days in the wilderness and found no water.' Those who explain verses symbolically said: water means Torah, as it says, 'Ho, everyone who thirsts, come for water.' Since they went three days without Torah, they became weary. The נביאים among them arose and arranged that they should read on שבת, pause on Sunday, read on Monday, pause on Tuesday and Wednesday, read on Thursday, and pause on Friday, so they would never go three days without Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove its challenge. The ברייתא shows that Monday and Thursday reading goes all the way back to the time of the desert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the people found no water for three days. Water stands for Torah, so the ברייתא reads it as three days without Torah. The schedule the נביאים set up (שבת, Monday, Thursday) makes sure there is never a gap of three days. So the practice is much older than עזרא.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who explain פסוקים in a symbolic way
They became weary or worn out
They pause, they skip a day
They would stay or pass time (literally, spend the night)

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא does not argue with עזרא's list on its own. The גמרא is using it to show that the practice is older than עזרא, and the next step explains what עזרא actually added.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
"And they went three days in the wilderness
and did not find water":
Those who explain verses symbolically said:
Water means nothing other than Torah,
as it says: "Ho, everyone who thirsts, come for water."

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁהָלְכוּ שְׁלֹשֶׁת יָמִים בְּלֹא תּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: Since they went three days without Torah,
they became weary,
the prophets who were among them arose
and instituted for them that they should read on Shabbat,
and pause on Sunday,
and read on Monday,
and pause on Tuesday and Wednesday,
and read on Thursday,
and pause on Friday,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יָלִינוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים בְּלֹא תּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: so that they would not go three days without Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It gives the source that backs up the challenge in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that Monday and Thursday Torah reading existed before עזרא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on שמות 15:22, which reads 'water' as Torah based on ישעיהו 55:1.

steps.title: עזרא changed how much was read and by how many people
steps.stepSummary: The reading itself was old, but at first it was only three פסוקים (read by one man or by three men). עזרא made it three men and at least ten פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Originally they instituted one man reading three פסוקים, or alternatively three men reading three פסוקים, matching כהנים, לוים and ישראלים. עזרא came and instituted three men and ten פסוקים, matching the ten בטלנין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. עזרא did not start the reading; he changed how it is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original practice had three פסוקים. There are two versions of who read them: one man, or three men. Either way, the number three matched כהנים, לוים and ישראלים. עזרא's new תקנה was a fixed format of three readers and ten פסוקים, to match the ten בטלנין of a town. So his name on the list is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: Man / men (here, the people called up to read)
Men free from work who are always available for community needs

steps.whatToRemember: The basic Monday and Thursday reading is older than עזרא. His תקנה was the format of three people called up, reading at least ten פסוקים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for today's practice on Monday and Thursday: three people are called up, and together they read at least ten פסוקים.

phrases.english: Originally they instituted
one man reading three verses,

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי תְּלָתָא גַּבְרֵי – תְּלָתָא פְּסוּקֵי,
phrases.english: or alternatively, three men reading three verses,
corresponding to Kohanim, Levites and Israelites;
he came,
and instituted three men and ten verses,
corresponding to the ten idle men.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It resolves the challenge from steps 6 and 7 by separating the old practice from עזרא's addition.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the practice: the old basic reading versus עזרא's new format.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought עזרא's תקנה was reading on Monday and Thursday at all, which would clash with the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The reading itself came from the נביאים. עזרא set the format of three men and ten פסוקים.

steps.title: Why courts sit on Monday and Thursday
steps.stepSummary: The next תקנה is that courts judge on Monday and Thursday, because people are already in town to hear the Torah reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that courts judge on Monday and Thursday: because people are around then, since they come to hear the reading of the ספר תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the third תקנה on עזרא's list and gives its reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the previous step. Since people from the countryside come into town for the Monday and Thursday reading, it is easy for a בית דין to hear their cases on those same days.

keyTerms.meaning: They are found, they are present

phrases.english: And they judge on Monday and Thursday:
because people are around,
since they come to hear the reading of the Book.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the second תקנה, the גמרא explains the third, which depends on the Monday and Thursday reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Courts sit on Monday and Thursday, because people are already in town for the Torah reading.

steps.title: Laundry on Thursday for the honor of שבת
steps.stepSummary: עזרא set up that people should wash clothes on Thursday so that they have clean clothes for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the rule that people should do laundry on Thursday was made out of respect for שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next תקנה on עזרא's list and gives its reason. Clothes are washed on Thursday because of כבוד שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the earlier items, the גמרא simply names the reason behind the rule. If you wash on Thursday, the clothes are clean and dry in time for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: the fifth day of the week, which is Thursday
honoring שבת, for example by having clean clothes

phrases.english: And that people should do laundry on Thursday:
this is because of the honor of Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next item on the same list of עזרא's תקנות, after courts sitting on Monday and Thursday.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Laundry is done on Thursday so that there are clean clothes for שבת.

steps.title: Eating garlic on Friday because of marital intimacy
steps.stepSummary: עזרא set up eating garlic on ערב שבת because it helps with עונה, which is set for Friday night.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the rule that people should eat garlic on Friday was made because of עונה, the time for marital relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for the next תקנה: garlic on ערב שבת. It connects the rule to עונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Garlic was thought to strengthen a man for marital relations, and Friday night is the set time for them. This step gives only the reason. The next step brings a פסוק to show that Friday night really is that time.

keyTerms.meaning: the set time for marital relations between husband and wife

phrases.english: And that people should eat garlic on Shabbat eve:
this is because of marital relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next item on the list of תקנות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Garlic is eaten on ערב שבת because Friday night is the time of עונה.

steps.title: A verse shows Friday night is the time for intimacy
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'who gives his fruit in its season' is read as describing someone who keeps marital relations every Friday night.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'that gives its fruit in its season.' One of four Sages said that this means a man who has marital relations every Friday night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק from תהלים to support the idea that Friday night is the time for עונה. It is not sure which Sage taught this reading, so it lists four possible names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in its season' (בְּעִתּוֹ) are read as a fixed, regular time, and that time is Friday night. This explains why garlic, which helps with עונה, belongs on ערב שבת. The list of names only shows doubt about who said the teaching. It does not change what the teaching says.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is written in a פסוק
in its proper time or season
and some say it was this person who said it
a polite way of saying 'has marital relations'

steps.confusionAlert: The four names (רבי יהודה, רב נחמן, רב כהנא, רבי יוחנן) are not four Sages arguing with each other. The גמרא gives one teaching and is unsure which of them said it.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'That brings forth its fruit in its season.'
And Rabbi Yehuda said,
and some say it was Rav Naḥman,
and some say it was Rav Kahana,
and some say it was Rabbi Yoḥanan:
This refers to one who has marital relations
from Shabbat eve to Shabbat eve.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reason given in step 11 by showing that Friday night is the set time for עונה.
steps.raayaObject: That Friday night is the fixed time for עונה, which explains garlic on ערב שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 1:3, 'אשר פריו יתן בעתו', as read by רבי יהודה (or רב נחמן, רב כהנא, or רבי יוחנן).

steps.title: A side teaching on the benefits of garlic
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists five good things about garlic, and some add two more: it brings love and removes jealousy.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: five things were said about garlic. It fills you up, warms the body, makes the face shine, increases a man's seed, and kills lice in the intestines. Some say it also brings in love and takes away jealousy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps aside for a moment to quote a ברייתא about garlic's benefits. This fits here because the topic is the garlic תקנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of the list is about health. 'Increases seed' ties back to עונה, which was the reason for the garlic תקנה. The יש אומרים add emotional benefits: it brings love and removes jealousy.

keyTerms.meaning: it makes the face shine or glow

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, חֲמִשָּׁה דְּבָרִים נֶאֶמְרוּ בַּשּׁוּם:
phrases.english: The Sages taught: Five things were said about garlic:
It satisfies, it warms, and it makes the face shine,
and it increases seed,
and it kills lice that are in the intestines.
phrases.notes: He means tiny worms or parasites inside the stomach.

phrases.english: And some say: it brings in love
and takes out jealousy.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, חֲמִשָּׁה דְּבָרִים נֶאֶמְרוּ בַּשּׁוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side note that grows out of the garlic תקנה and supports its link to עונה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Garlic fills, warms, brightens the face, increases seed, and kills intestinal parasites. Some add that it brings love and removes jealousy.

steps.title: Women bake early so bread is ready for the poor
steps.stepSummary: עזרא set up that a woman should get up early to bake, so that bread is already available when poor people come asking.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the rule that a woman should get up early and bake was made so that bread would be on hand for the poor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the list of עזרא's תקנות after the garlic side note. It gives the reason for the early baking rule: to help the poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Poor people went door to door asking for bread in the morning. If the baking was done early, there would be bread to give them right away, so they would not leave with nothing. The reason here is kindness to others, not שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: bread that is available and ready

phrases.english: And that a woman should rise early and bake:
so that bread should be available for poor people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the garlic side note, returns to the next item on the list of עזרא's תקנות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women bake early in the morning so that bread is ready to give to the poor.

steps.title: A woman should wear a סינר for modesty
steps.stepSummary: Another enactment of עזרא: a woman should wear a סינר, because of צניעות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that a woman should wear a סינר, because of modesty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its list of עזרא's enactments. This one says a woman should wear a protective undergarment, a סינר, for the sake of צניעות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike some earlier items, this one gives no פסוק and needs no proof. The reason is stated right away: modesty. The גמרא accepts it without question and moves to the next item.

keyTerms.meaning: wears tied around her, girds herself
an apron-like undergarment worn for modesty

phrases.english: And that a woman should wear a סינר
phrases.notes: This is a protective garment worn under her clothing, like a covering apron.

phrases.english: because of modesty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the list of עזרא's enactments, with its reason explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עזרא set up that a woman should wear a סינר, for modesty.

steps.title: Combing before immersion is already a Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The next enactment is that a woman combs her hair and then immerses. The גמרא objects: that is already required by the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that a woman should comb her hair and then immerse. But that is a Torah law!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next enactment, combing before טבילה, and immediately challenges it. If the Torah already requires this, how can it be counted as עזרא's enactment?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תקנה of עזרא should be something new that was not already required. Combing is meant to remove anything in the hair that blocks the water, and the גמרא claims the Torah already demands that. So listing it as עזרא's enactment seems to make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: combs or washes out her hair
from the Torah, a Torah-level law

phrases.english: And that a woman should comb her hair and then immerse
But that is from the Torah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the next item on the list and attacks it as already being a Torah law.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that combing before טבילה is an enactment of עזרא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rabbinic enactment cannot simply repeat what the Torah already commands. Removing anything in the hair that blocks the water is already a Torah law.

steps.title: A ברייתא proves the hair must be free of anything blocking
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'ורחץ את בשרו במים' to mean nothing may block the water, and the word את includes the hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: 'And he shall bathe his flesh in water' means nothing may block between his flesh and the water. 'את בשרו' includes what is attached to his flesh, and what is that? Hair!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge with a ברייתא. It shows from a פסוק that the Torah already requires the water to reach even the hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ורחץ את בשרו במים' teach that nothing may block (חציצה) between the body and the water. The extra word את adds something attached to the body, which is the hair. So the Torah itself already covers the hair, and the challenge from the previous step is now proven.

keyTerms.meaning: blocks, comes between (the water and the body)

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
'And he shall bathe his flesh in water'
teaches that nothing should block
between his flesh and the water.
'את his flesh'
phrases.notes: The ברייתא reads the little word את as adding something more than just the skin.

phrases.english: includes what is attached to his flesh,
and what is that? Hair!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the challenge that combing is a Torah law.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the Torah already requires the hair to be free of anything that blocks the water.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ויקרא 14:9, using the word את to include the hair.

steps.title: The Torah only requires checking the hair
steps.stepSummary: The answer begins: the Torah requires checking the hair for knots or dirt that would block the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: From the Torah, one must check in case hair is knotted, or in case there is something disgusting in it, because of blocking;
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer the challenge by defining exactly what the Torah requires. The sentence is not finished here; it is setting up what עזרא added beyond the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer narrows the Torah law: it only requires checking (לעיוני) for knotted hair or dirt, since those block the water. That leaves room for עזרא's enactment to be something more than just checking, and the גמרא will spell that out next.

keyTerms.meaning: something blocking the water from the body

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop here thinking the answer is complete. This line only explains the Torah's requirement; what עזרא added comes right after.

phrases.english: They answer:
From the Torah, one must check
in case some hair is knotted,
or in case there is something disgusting there,
because that would block the water;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of steps 16-17 by limiting what the Torah requires.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the exact scope of the Torah law so the rabbinic enactment can add to it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Torah already requires combing, so עזרא added nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah requires only checking the hair for knots or dirt; עזרא's enactment (explained next) goes beyond that.
